label: Sequence starts with z/x/n/f/c/s; fires on certain later inputs (i,u,h,m,b,p,2,d) and at <DEL>
explanation: Low end of candidate unit 49. It mostly fires in the input phase from step 2 up to and including the <DEL> step (t <= L), and depends on two things together. (1) The first original token: rates are highest when it is z, x, n, f or c (3-4x lift), then s. A second token in that set helps a little too. (2) The current input token: <DEL> (3.5x, 35% of mass) and i, u, h, m, b, p, 2, d. The strongest activations (near max) come at <DEL> in short sequences that start with z, e.g. z n u <DEL>. Firing is strongest at t=3-4 and weak from step L+1 onward (copy phase, ~0.4x lift). It is almost never active at t=0-1. It fires more on the first occurrence of a token and less when the sequence has many digits. It looks like a graded mix of first-token identity and current-token identity rather than a crisp rule: the conjunction gets dev precision 0.65 and recall 0.43 (mass recall 0.60). Many smaller activations fall outside the listed sets, and plenty of predicted steps stay inactive.
